title: Cell fractionation and ultracentrifugation; Dissection and tissue studies
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: PR05b#t2 term and clue written for the game; PR05b#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE06#t1 term and clue written for the game; PR05a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE06#N.3, PR05a#N.9, PR05b#N.11, CE06#N.7.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Vein
items.clue: Vessel with a thin wall that collapses flat.

items.label: Artery
items.clue: Vessel with a thick, elastic wall that stays open.

items.label: Homogeniser
items.clue: A blender used to break open the cells of chopped tissue

items.label: Pith
items.clue: Tissue in the middle of a stem, inside the ring of vascular bundles.

questions.stem: Liver tissue is homogenised in an ice-cold, isotonic, buffered solution. Why must the solution be isotonic?

options.text: So the liver cells do not burst before the organelles can be collected.
So that enzymes released from the cells are denatured and cannot digest the organelles.
So that the pH of the homogenate stays constant while the organelles are being separated.
So organelles do not gain or lose water by osmosis, and do not burst or shrivel.

questions.explanation: With equal water potential inside and outside, there is no net movement of water, so the organelles keep their structure.

questions.stem: A student draws a cell from an electron micrograph of a gland that secretes enzymes, and must annotate each structure with its function. Which annotation is correct?

options.text: Golgi apparatus — synthesises the enzymes that the cell will later secrete by exocytosis.
Rough endoplasmic reticulum — synthesises proteins that are destined for secretion from the cell.
Microvilli — beat rhythmically to move the secreted enzymes along the surface of the cell.
Secretory vesicles — break down worn-out organelles inside the cell using the hydrolytic enzymes they hold.

questions.stem: A student dissects a set of sheep's lungs. Near the lungs she finds two tubes side by side. Tube P has C-shaped rings of cartilage in its wall and stays open when empty. Tube Q has a thin, soft wall with no cartilage and collapses flat. Which identification do these observations best support?

options.text: P is an artery: it has the thicker wall and stays open, as arteries do.
P is a bronchus, held open by its cartilage; Q is a blood vessel.
Q is an artery: blood at high pressure needs a wide, soft-walled vessel.
Q is a vein, because it carries blood that is low in oxygen.

questions.explanation: Structure identifies it: C-shaped cartilage keeps airways open. A thin wall that collapses fits a vein, such as a pulmonary vein.

questions.stem: Which conclusion do the data support?

options.text: Most mitochondria are in pellet 2, but pellet 2 is not a pure sample of mitochondria.
Pellet 1 contains nuclei and nothing else.
Mitochondria are the densest organelles, as they are found in the first pellet.
Ribosomes are larger than mitochondria, as they need the fastest spin to be collected.

questions.explanation: Pellet 2 holds 84% of the mitochondrial enzyme, but also 5% of the DNA and 6% of the rRNA, so some nuclear material and ribosomes are mixed in.
